title: What broke running agents on free-tier quotas
hook: I treated every 429 the same and it cost me a day
subtitle: Lessons learned from building a personal multi-agent AI assistant

slides.heading: The swarm ate my whole quota
slides.body: Running 13 specialist agents in parallel pushed a single query to roughly 70,000 tokens, triggering rate limits almost immediately. I had to cap each tool result at 1,500 characters and compact conversation history to mitigate this.

slides.heading: Not all 429s are equal
slides.body: A per-minute limit clears in 60 seconds, so backing off and retrying works. A per-day limit does not clear until midnight, so every retry burns an attempt you cannot get back. Same status code, opposite correct response.

slides.heading: Latency was 8x over budget
slides.body: The median response time was 6.7 seconds, with a p90 of 24.0 seconds. Only 5 out of 22 runs finished in under a second, which is far from the 800 milliseconds required for a real-time voice interface.

slides.heading: Model fallback across providers matters
slides.body: My model fallback chain consists of 4 models from different providers. When one provider's daily quota is exhausted, every model from that provider is exhausted at once. I had to deliberately cross providers to ensure reliability.

slides.heading: A colon broke the build
slides.body: My agent wrote posts with unquoted colons in the frontmatter, which is invalid YAML. I had to quote every generated string to fix this issue.

slides.heading: Two repos, one mistake
slides.body: The agent wrote posts into one repo, but the website read from a different repo. I had to connect the two to ensure automation was complete.

slides.heading: Measure and monitor latency
slides.body: To avoid the pitfalls I encountered, measure and monitor latency to ensure it meets your requirements. Implement rate limiting and model fallback strategies to avoid quota exhaustion.

slides.heading: Test your model's limitations
slides.body: Test your model's ability to handle structured tool calling and escape generated content to avoid formatting issues.

outro: Go back to slide 1 to learn more
caption:
Building a personal multi-agent AI assistant on free-tier quotas was a challenge. 
I encountered several issues, from latency to rate limits. 
Here's what I learned and how you can avoid the same pitfalls.
